answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded stake with slashing: each agent locks capital at a staking jetty before its vote counts, and influence is anchored to one verified vertex instead of raw identity count. Caught fraud burns the bond, so an attacker spinning up a thousand sparrow identities must post a separate bond for every one and forfeits the whole pile when detected. The attack cost therefore scales linearly with the number of fake agents while an honest participant pays only once, making a Sybil flood economically irrational.
